question: What fluid-dynamic readouts (flow velocity, shear) matter for pronephric filtration onset, and what mesh formats (.vtu/.cgns) carry them?
direct_answer:
For pronephric filtration onset, the fluid-dynamic readouts that matter are: (1) flow velocity — cell/segment/node-indexed flow vectors quantifying the magnitude and direction of fluid movement through the developing nephron; (2) pressure fields, which set up the filtration gradient across the glomerular/tubular wall; and (3) wall shear stress, which is derived from the velocity field near tubular/glomerular surfaces and is a mechanically relevant cue for filtration and epithelial maturation. In the RN7 niche ("Mecánica activa y dinámica de fluidos"), these scalar/vector fields — flow vectors, velocity, and pressure — are carried as cell/segment/node-indexed tabular data in .csv/.tsv format, while the spatial domain on which they are defined is provided as high-density 3D meshes. NOTE: the retrieved RN7 description is truncated and does NOT explicitly confirm .vtu or .cgns as the mesh container formats, nor does it explicitly list "shear" as a stored field — those specifics are not verifiable from the evidence provided. The CORPUS-2026-0003 chunk confirms the zebrafish pronephros as an in vivo model for studying when/how the nephron develops but does not itself specify fluid-dynamic quantities or mesh formats.</parameter>
